items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: Yeah. With Cameron. We’ll do it. We just did it last week in Europe, a couple of weeks ago.

ctx.x: Yeah. With Cameron. We’ll do it. We just did it last week in Europe, a couple of weeks ago.
Do you like to listen to your own recordings?

items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But I love working with his Here and Now band.

ctx.x: Oh. I still don‟t listen to myself. Nah, [inaudible]. Brown, C.: She can‟t bear to listen to anything that she‟s on.

But I love working with his Here and Now band. I didn‟t think I would. Because I thought some of it was too out for me. But somehow I managed to get what, get my thing in there and be, and be honest with the way I felt it and approached the music. And uh, I didn‟t know about Don Byron. [laughs] Don Byron‟s out. But somebody wrote something on my, uh, on an e-mail or something or somewhere in Facebook or something that said, “You know, Sheila, you oughta do something with Don Byron.” [laughs] And I, and I laughed…

He really is. And you know. And thanks to Cameron, I got to find that out. Otherwise, I never would have known. Brown, C.: Well, we did, we did a one European tour with that quartet with Don and Tony Jefferson and Sheila.
